items.body:
## Component and environment

- ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop app, Windows 11 x64.
- Installed package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`.
- The relevant executable is `ChatGPT.exe`, with display description `Codex`. Separate CLI `codex.exe` processes were also present; the display name alone does not identify the executable or a chat.

## Reproduction and user-visible behavior

1. Restart the independent execution-process monitor, then launch the desktop app.
2. Observe substantial incoming network traffic. The user saw a Task Manager row labelled Codex using approximately 100 Mbps.
3. The whole desktop app unexpectedly exits. This happened again after restarting it, during investigation.

Expected: The app remains open. If a download or background operation fails, it should recover without terminating the entire app.

Actual: Two browser-type Crashpad markers coincide with the app and its monitored related processes disappearing.

## Verified incident timeline

All times below are on 2026-10-08, Asia/Seoul (UTC+09:00).

- 18:38:40: PC-adapter receive traffic rose to about 8.60 MB/s, later about 12.87 MB/s.
- 18:39:29.652947: Crashpad sidecar recorded `{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}`. At the next monitor sample, 18:39:30, the app's parent PID 2972 and related processes were absent.
- 18:40:35: After a user-reported manual termination of a busy Codex-labelled row during the next run, the monitor recorded child PID 27228 disappearing and child PID 27824 appearing under the same surviving parent PID 20280. PID 27228 is a candidate for the manually terminated row; the user did not record its PID, so this identification is not certain.
- Network receive traffic briefly fell after this child replacement.
- 18:42:25: High receive traffic resumed, reaching approximately 12.89 MB/s before the next exit.
- 18:43:08.705781: A second sidecar recorded the same browser-type crash marker. At 18:43:10, parent PID 20280, child PID 27824, and the other monitored related processes were all absent.

## Evidence and limitations

The full public investigation MD, the address-free CSV extract, both Crashpad sidecars, and the evidence manifest are included below. The connector does not expose a binary-attachment upload endpoint, so the file contents are reproduced in the issue body rather than claiming that the ZIP was uploaded. Source log line numbers are retained.

- Network byte counters are for the selected PC network adapter, NOT per-process counters. They corroborate timing, not which process transferred the bytes or what was transferred.
- PID-specific TCP connection counts were recorded, but no payload contents, full command lines, authentication data, or chat contents are included.
- Monitor sampling interval is approximately 5 seconds. A process being absent does not establish its exact exit time, the exit initiator, or shutdown ordering.
- Crashpad sidecar timestamps are file modification times, not embedded timestamps. The sidecars contain no PID, exception code, faulting module, or stack trace. No `.dmp` was available in the inspected Crashpad directories.
- A bounded Windows Application log lookup for event IDs 1000/1001/1002/1026, 18:38–18:45 KST, returned no matching events. This does not invalidate the Crashpad markers.
- The responsible chat, download target, direct crash cause, and whether the resumed transfer was the same operation remain unknown. No Windows fault, `node_repl.exe` fault, or particular chat is established as the cause.

Please investigate the browser-process crash and the background network operation around these timestamps. Please advise which additional diagnostics would identify the operation and provide a stack trace.

## Possibly related reports

- #52029 reports a Windows desktop exit on the same package version. No dump or faulting module was available in this investigation, so the same cause is not established.
- #52007 describes tool-initialization failures. Browser initialization also failed separately with `node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly` and `windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors` when trying to report this incident; its relationship to the app crashes is unknown.

This report adds independently recorded receive-traffic and process-lifecycle evidence. Please consolidate if appropriate.

# ChatGPT/Codex 자동 종료 조사 — 2026-10-08 재현 기록

모든 시각은 한국시간(KST)이다. 실행 도구 모니터 v2.2의 18:38:20부터 18:44:35까지를 사건 분석 범위로 삼았다. 원본 로그는 이후에도 추가되는 파일이므로 아래 줄 번호는 이미 기록된 해당 사건을 가리킨다.

## 확인된 결론

1. **두 번의 자동 종료에 대응하는 실제 앱 충돌 표식이 있다.** 18:39:29 및 18:43:08에 Crashpad가 `capture_kind=crash`, `ptype=browser`를 기록했고, 바로 다음 모니터 측정에서 앱과 관련 프로세스가 모두 사라졌다. 단순히 창이 숨겨진 상황으로 설명되지 않는다.
2. **사용자가 두 번째 실행에서 강제 종료한 항목의 유력한 후보는 PID 27228이다.** 18:40:35 측정에서 이 프로세스가 사라지고, 같은 부모 PID 20280 아래에 PID 27824가 새로 관측됐다. 부모 앱은 계속 실행 중이었다. 사용자가 PID나 종료 시각을 기록하지 않았으므로 수동 종료 대상이라고 확정하지는 않는다.
3. **중간의 통신 감소는 지속되지 않았다.** 위 교체 뒤 통신량이 줄었으나 18:42:25부터 다시 크게 늘었고, 18:43:08에 두 번째 앱 충돌 표식이 남았다.
4. **다운로드 대상과 충돌을 일으킨 코드까지 특정한 것은 아니다.** 현재 모니터의 바이트 수는 PC의 선택된 네트워크 어댑터 전체 값이다. 특정 PID의 전송량이나 전송 내용이 아니다. 대량 통신과 앱 충돌의 시간상 연관성은 확인됐지만 인과관계는 미확인이다.

## 근거 파일

### 실행 도구 모니터 원본

`<LOCAL_MONITOR_FOLDER>\NodeMonitor\Logs\node-monitor-20261008T0938204895970Z-19724-c5c6eaba02914993bbe313bf5abd1812-000001.jsonl`

아래 표의 줄 번호는 이 파일의 1부터 시작하는 줄 번호다. 로그의 UTC 시각을 KST로 변환했다. 측정 시각과 로그 기록 시각 사이에 수십 밀리초 차이가 있으므로 표는 초 단위로 표시한다.

### 앱 자체 충돌 표식

1. `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Codex\web\Codex\Crashpad\reports\7eecc13d-42fc-4d3f-a5ae-01ad37383fb3_sidecar.json`
   - 파일 수정 시각: 2026-10-08 18:39:29.652947 KST
   - 60바이트, 전체 내용은 1행: `{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}`
2. `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Codex\web\Codex\Crashpad\reports\cb95bf96-5df5-4f0a-b7f3-3d492203b5d0_sidecar.json`
   - 파일 수정 시각: 2026-10-08 18:43:08.705781 KST
   - 60바이트, 전체 내용은 1행: `{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}`

위 시각은 JSON 내부 시각 필드가 아니라 파일 수정 시각이다. `browser` 종류의 충돌을 직접 확인할 수 있지만 이 JSON에는 충돌 PID, 예외 코드, 문제 모듈이나 호출 스택이 없다. 따라서 부모 PID 2972/20280과의 연결은 모니터 시각 대조에 따른 것이며 sidecar 내부 PID로 확인한 것은 아니다.

패키지의 `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Roaming\Codex\web\Codex\Crashpad`에서도 같은 이름·크기·시각의 파일을 확인했다. 별도의 추가 충돌로 중복 계산하지 않는다. 조회 당시 Crashpad 파일 목록에서 `.dmp` 파일은 확인되지 않았다. 해당 범위의 목록 조회에는 접근 오류가 없었다.

### Windows 오류 기록

Windows Application 로그를 2026-10-08 18:38:00–18:45:00, 이벤트 ID 1000/1001/1002/1026으로 읽기 전용 조회했다. 해당 조건에 맞는 이벤트가 없다는 결과가 반환됐다. 이는 위 Crashpad 충돌을 부정하는 근거가 아니며 Windows 전체 로그나 모든 오류 종류를 점검한 결과도 아니다.

## 작업 관리자의 ‘Codex’ 표시를 해석할 때 주의할 점

이 사건의 PID 27228과 27824는 로그에서 표시 이름이 `Codex`이고 실제 실행 파일은 다음 경로의 `ChatGPT.exe`다.

`C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\app\ChatGPT.exe`

따라서 화면의 ‘Codex’라는 글자만 보고 CLI 실행 파일 `codex.exe`나 특정 채팅 작업자라고 단정하면 안 된다. 실제 CLI `codex.exe`도 별도로 존재하며 이번 로그에서 구분되어 기록됐다. 자식 프로세스의 정확한 내부 역할이나 소유 채팅은 이번 조사에서 확인되지 않았다.

## 추론과 미확인 사항

- **추론:** 한 자식이 사라진 직후 같은 부모 아래 새 자식이 생겼고, 통신이 잠시 줄었다가 재발했다. 앱이 보조 프로세스를 다시 띄우고 통신 작업을 재시도하는 흐름일 가능성이 있다. 동일 작업의 재시도인지, 다른 통신 작업인지는 미확인이다.
- **미확인:** 어떤 파일·모델·업데이트·채팅 자료를 받았는지, 실제 수신 담당 PID, 충돌을 일으킨 함수 및 오류 코드. 현재 수집 방식은 이를 기록하지 않는다.
- **미확인:** Windows 자체 문제, 앱 업데이트의 특정 결함, `node_repl.exe` 잠금 오류와 이번 충돌의 인과관계. 현재 자료로 어느 하나를 원인으로 확정할 수 없다.
- **확인 한계:** 모니터는 약 5초 간격의 성공한 목록을 비교한다. ‘사라짐’은 그 측정에서 더 이상 보이지 않았다는 뜻이며 정확한 종료 순간·종료 주체·프로세스 간 종료 순서를 뜻하지 않는다. TCP 연결 수가 많다는 것만으로 해당 PID의 전송 바이트 수를 알 수 없다. UDP/QUIC 및 측정 사이에 끝난 연결은 이 자료에 포함되지 않을 수 있다.

## 다음 작업자에게 필요한 내용

증거 확보의 다음 목표는 두 사건 시각의 **앱 충돌 상세 정보와 대량 수신 작업의 정체를 연결하는 것**이다. 현재 자료만으로 특정 채팅을 중지하거나 `node_repl.exe`를 닫으면 해결된다고 안내하지 않는다. 자식 프로세스 강제 종료 뒤 앱이 살아 있었던 것은 확인됐지만 잠시 후 대량 통신과 앱 충돌이 재발했기 때문이다.

추가 수집을 한다면 프로세스 종류를 구분하는 앱 진단 정보, 해당 시간대의 다운로드/업데이트 작업 식별자, 예외 코드 또는 호출 스택을 우선 확보해야 한다. 이는 이번 조사에서 확보하거나 실행한 사항이 아니다. 캐시 삭제·재설치·방화벽 변경을 해결책으로 검증한 기록도 없다. 외부 전달 시에는 네트워크 주소 등 원본 로그에 포함될 수 있는 개인정보를 검토해야 한다.

이번 조사는 기존 로그·메타데이터·오류 기록 읽기와 이 MD 추가만 수행했다. 앱 실행 파일과 모니터 코드, 게임 프로젝트, 기존 MD, 저장 파일, Windows 설정을 변경하지 않았고 프로세스를 종료하지 않았다. 빌드·게임 실행·회귀 검사를 수행하거나 통과했다고 주장하지 않는다.

## Problem
Codex CLI 0.161.0 on Windows fails to run commands in `read-only` and `workspace-write` sandbox modes with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`. Running commands outside the sandbox succeeds. The failure reproduces with the desktop app closed.

## Reproduction
Run `codex.cmd --no-daemon --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval never`, then ask it to execute `Write-Output "Codex CLI OK"`.

## Evidence
ProcMon shows `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` receiving `SHARING VIOLATION` when opening the user profile directory and the active `cua_node/.../bin/node_repl.exe` runtime with `Maximum Allowed` access. Restarting, rebuilding runtime directories, and running CLI without desktop did not resolve the problem.

Codex desktop version: 26.1002.7124.0. Original ProcMon traces are withheld to avoid disclosing private local system information. The process responsible for the conflicting file access is not yet identified.

We are evaluating one application-owned, read-only telemetry function through a separately hosted, non-elevated Codex App Server over stdio. The model thread would have no execution environments, shell, general network, MCP, browser, or Computer Use capabilities. The existing Desktop setup and all managed policies must remain unchanged.

**Installed identities**

- Codex App Server: `0.162.0-alpha.2`
- App Server executable SHA-256: `3553cd6e7df5a093d8cb8301cd8088a57e0971aba71ddbe0e67f7f44a15cdf68`
- Computer Use package: `@oai/sky` `0.7.6`
- Runtime directory identifier: `3dd31cfff853001c`
- Configured notification: `codex-computer-use.exe turn-ended`
- Callback SHA-256: `63c98c4dd5d707df3240a04da1fbf7fe47ff0622cf757ee886eee96434d4e17a`
- The callback has a valid OpenAI OpCo, LLC Authenticode signature.
- Desktop startup logs show the `computer-use-native-pipe` component ensuring or repairing this notification setting.

The experimental host stopped on this setting before creating a thread or model turn. We have not executed the callback, changed configuration, or inspected proprietary binary internals.

Please provide a version-specific supported contract or published implementation reference addressing:

1. What does `turn-ended` do, and which lifecycle or security responsibilities does it fulfill? Which success, failure, or interruption events dispatch it?
2. Does a separately hosted App Server dispatch it when Computer Use is disabled and unused? Does it require Desktop environment variables, native-pipe context, or existing sessions? Can it affect sessions belonging to the Desktop process?
3. Which fields of the notification JSON does it consume or retain? What files, processes, IPC endpoints, or network destinations can this subcommand access? Does it parse message text as anything other than data?
4. Under which Windows token and integrity level is it launched, and does the launch path apply restrictions independent of the model’s tool sandbox?
5. Is it mandatory for this independent host, policy-enforced, a no-op without an active Computer Use session, or safely optional? If omission is supported, what documented per-host configuration preserves Desktop lifecycle and security behavior and all managed policy?

We need either a bounded coexistence contract or an explicitly supported independent-host configuration. We are not asking to relax sandbox, approval, Desktop, telemetry, or network protections.

Related public context: [issue #33254](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33254) discusses the older Windows `turn-ended` helper, but does not answer the version-specific questions above.

items.body:
## Summary
Local command execution is blocked before the requested command starts by `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`. The sandbox refresh attempts a root-only ACL update on the bundled CUA `node_repl.exe`, but Windows returns a sharing violation (`os error 32`). This appears to match #52046; reporting an additional case with the relevant log details.

## Environment
- Desktop app version reported by the app updater: 26.1002.52244, build 13536, release channel prod. The updater reported up_to_date when checked.
- Windows desktop environment; exact OS build has not been collected.
- Sandbox setup binary: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9691020b546a15b2\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe`.
- Affected runtime: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe`.

## Reproduction in the affected environment
1. Open an existing local workspace in the desktop app.
2. Request a minimal read-only PowerShell operation, such as `Get-Item -LiteralPath <existing workspace ZIP>`.
3. The operation never starts. Process creation is rejected with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`.
4. Repeated attempts over October 7–8, 2026 produce the same initialization failure.

## Relevant sandbox log (personal paths anonymized)
```text
setup refresh: spawning ...\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe (payload_len=3436)
failed to grant non-inheriting read-attributes ACE on user profile <USERPROFILE>: open ACL target for root-only update: El proceso no tiene acceso al archivo porque está siendo utilizado por otro proceso. (os error 32); continuing setup
read-acl-only mode: applying read ACLs
read ACL run completed
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on <LOCALAPPDATA>\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe: open ACL target for root-only update: El proceso no tiene acceso al archivo porque está siendo utilizado por otro proceso. (os error 32)
setup refresh: processed 3 write roots (read roots delegated)
setup refresh completed with errors
setup error: setup refresh had errors
setup refresh: exited with status ExitStatus(ExitStatus(1))
```
`setup_error.json` contains only:
```json
{"code":"helper_unknown_error","message":"setup refresh had errors"}
```

## Troubleshooting and limits of available evidence
- Retried read-only commands repeatedly; none reached execution.
- Reset the Node REPL session through its reset tool; reset returned success, but shell setup still failed.
- The user confirmed terminating the Node helper task. A subsequent sandbox log still identified the same sharing violation on node_repl.exe.
- App/Windows restarts were suggested; the user returned requesting checks, which still failed. A complete Windows restart was not explicitly confirmed, so this report does not claim that it was conclusively tested.
- We have not identified which process holds the conflicting handle.
- No ACLs or runtime files were deleted or changed as a workaround.

## Expected and actual behavior
Expected: sandbox setup succeeds and permitted read-only commands can execute.
Actual: all local shell work is blocked during setup, preventing file inspection, edits, builds and tests. The underlying sharing violation is visible only in the sandbox log, while the tool returns the generic setup refresh message.

Please investigate the runtime ACL refresh/locking interaction and expose the affected path and underlying Windows error more directly in the user-facing diagnostic.

### What issue are you seeing?

In a chat with a cloud environment selected, a plain question about the repository's contents is answered instantly from general knowledge. Codex does not open the workspace and replies by asking me to send the documents, even though they are in the checked-out repo.

My use case: a repository of Markdown/PDF documents that a non-technical person should be able to ask questions about without mentioning the repository in every message.

None of the places where I could put a "check the repo first" instruction changed the behavior:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Publishing the environment (it was a draft) | no effect |
| Rule as the first paragraph of the environment's Start skill | no effect (see #50879) |
| Codex custom instructions (Settings → Personalization) | no effect (related: #27705) |
| Turning off "Quick answers" | no effect |
| A Page pointing to `/workspace/<repo>` | no effect |
| `AGENTS.md` in the repo root | not loaded: the session starts in `/workspace`, one level above the checkout |

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a cloud environment for a repo that contains documents and publish it. The repo is checked out at `/workspace/<repo>`; the session starts in `/workspace`.
2. Open a new chat with that environment selected.
3. Ask a question that can only be answered from the files, without mentioning the repo, e.g. "Which invoices are still unpaid?"

Observed:
- Effort "Light" and "Medium": immediate reply asking me to send the documents. No tool calls, no file access.
- Effort "High": ~30 s, searched Pages only, replied "nothing found in the available materials".
- Effort "High" + explicit "look at the files in the repository": answered correctly, but via the GitHub integration rather than the environment.

When asked in a fresh chat what it received at session start, the model said: no user custom instructions in its context; only a generic `cloud-environment-runtime` skill it had not opened; environment status `starting`, environment name not passed, working directory `/workspace`; Pages skills available immediately, shell/file tools not in the explicit tool list. These are the model's own statements from one session, not a verified description of the internals.

### What is the expected behavior?

When an environment is selected, at least one of:

- the model is told that an environment with files is attached, and checks it before replying "please send the documents";
- `AGENTS.md` from the checked-out repo is loaded even though the session starts in `/workspace`;
- Codex custom instructions and the environment's Start skill are reliably in the initial context.

### Additional information

Related: #50879 (Start skill missing from task context), #27705 (custom instructions not injected), #51110.

Model shown in the picker: GPT-6.1 Sol. Plan: Pro. Date: 2026-10-07.

Hello OpenAI Support,

We observed intermittent inference failures in existing Codex Desktop threads on 2026-10-08. Please investigate the request-history compatibility error below. Execution has recovered in subsequent turns, including a real scheduled clock-only run, but we have not established a permanent fix or the exact trigger.

**Environment (read-only verified)**

- macOS 26.6.2, OS build 25G83; arm64.
- Desktop application version 26.1002.52244, application build 13536; bundle identifier com.openai.codex.
- Bundled codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2.
- Built-in OpenAI provider; affected turns used gpt-5.6-terra/high and gpt-6.1-sol/high.

**Exact error**

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "error": {
    "message": "Supplied input item IDs require persisted-item lookup that is not supported by rustponsesapi.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "input",
    "code": "unsupported_parameter"
  }
}
```

The listed failures occurred before tool execution. Thread A/B/C below are anonymous aliases for three existing local threads. Turn IDs are retained solely for official technical investigation. All timestamps are UTC on 2026-10-08; durations come from local turn metadata.

| Thread | Turn ID | UTC start–end | Model / effort | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 01a11abe-5d5e-7a93-b83c-6b30af542d04 | 09:00:45–09:00:53 | gpt-5.6-terra / high | Same HTTP 400; 7479 ms; no tools executed |
| B | 01a11ad0-050f-76d3-becd-fff1448e8b6b | 09:20:02–09:20:07 | gpt-5.6-terra / high | Same HTTP 400; 5079 ms; no tools executed |
| A | 01a11ad0-0656-7e11-b9d9-fc1889265386 | 09:20:03–09:28:12 | gpt-5.6-terra / high | Later continuation completed without this error |
| A | 01a11ad9-c50e-77c2-953e-29584c6c9cd5 | 09:30:41–09:30:54 | gpt-6.1-sol / high | Clock-only continuation completed; no model override supplied for this turn |
| C | 01a11add-bf89-7b00-9fc8-18282cfc0faa | 09:35:02–09:35:11 | gpt-6.1-sol / high | Same HTTP 400; 8597 ms; no tools executed |
| C | 01a11ae1-3d54-70c2-b1c2-fe3d5d9055d9 | 09:38:51–09:48:14 | gpt-6.1-sol / high | Subsequent same-thread continuation executed tools and completed |
| A | 01a11af3-cd84-7281-9e79-afe65c7cf081 | 09:59:07–09:59:39 | gpt-6.1-sol / high | Real scheduled clock-only turn completed; clock command exit 0; no turn error |

The last row's scheduled execution was corroborated by the recorded due time, scheduler last_run_at update, system heartbeat timestamp and new-turn timestamp; no separate turn_trigger field was available. It was not merely a manually submitted heartbeat-shaped message.

**Observed reproduction path (intermittent, not guaranteed)**

1. Continue an existing local thread using the supported Desktop/task interface.
2. Start a new turn with the selected model and high reasoning effort. Some initial continuation attempts fail with the exact error above before any tools execute.
3. Start a separate minimal continuation in the same original thread. Subsequent turns can execute successfully, including without resupplying the model setting.
4. A temporary real scheduler test using only a clock check also succeeded. Original thread identities, history and automation configuration were retained/restored.

We have not produced a deterministic synthetic reproducer. Raw prompts, request bodies and complete logs were deliberately not collected for this report.

**Relevant observations and measures**

- A supported model-setting change persisted, but gpt-6.1-sol also failed with the same error. Changing models is therefore not a sufficient fix.
- Two failing windows contained the client diagnostic `websocket reuse properties didn't match`. One successful continuation recorded `falling back to HTTP`; another successful continuation still used WebSocket. These are clues, not proof of a transport root cause.
- We cannot confirm that failure followed by continuation forces full-history replay or invalidates persisted-item references.
- Read-only feature inspection marks the old `responses_websockets`, `responses_websockets_v2` and `item_ids` flags as removed. A nonpersistent configuration-parse test rejected overriding `model_providers.openai.supports_websockets`, because `openai` is a reserved built-in provider ID. No provider configuration was changed.
- No histories were deleted, no new replacement threads were created, and no databases or rollout files were edited. No application/app-server restart was performed as a repair. We did not create a custom provider or alter authentication.

**Request to Support**

Please use the technical turn IDs to investigate the failed input-reference handling. Is this a known Desktop/app-server/backend compatibility issue? Can you recommend a supported remedy that preserves existing thread IDs and history, or identify a fixed application/runtime version? In particular, please clarify whether a supported retry or full-input replay control exists for this exact `unsupported_parameter` error with the built-in provider. We are not treating the distinct `previous_response_not_found` error as equivalent.

Current status: existing-thread and real scheduled execution have recovered in the observed tests; the underlying compatibility defect and its trigger remain unconfirmed. We are not claiming a backend patch or permanent resolution.

Thank you.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### Summarycommunity repackaging

When annotating selected text from an **assistant response** in Codex Desktop, pressing **Ctrl+Enter directly from the initial, still-open annotation editor** sends the selection/reference but **silently discards the note typed in that editor**.
Codex receives the selected response text without the user's accompanying comment.

This used to work as a one-step operation in approximately **August 2026**. The regression is suspected to have been introduced in **September 2026**, but the first affected build has not been identified.

### Scope / important UI distinction

This is the **assistant response-text annotation** flow in the main Codex chat, *not* the in-app browser annotation tool or a file-diff review comment.

The problem occurs specifically in the **first annotation input box that opens immediately after selecting a passage and clicking "add to chat"**. 
It is important to distinguish this editor from the editor opened later by closing the popover and clicking the numbered annotation marker/badge.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Codex Desktop conversation containing a completed assistant response.
2. Select a passage of the assistant's response and open its annotation input.
3. **Without first pressing Enter to commit the annotation**, type a note directly into the initial popover editor, for example: `Please explain this claim.`
4. While that note is still being edited, press **Ctrl+Enter** to send.
5. Inspect the submitted user turn / the information received by Codex.

### Actual behavior

- The selected assistant-response passage/reference is included.

- Exact current app build and OS: `26.1002.52244` on Gentoo Linux (ported via a [community repackaging](https://github.com/ilysenko/codex-desktop-linux/); this problematic behavior came even without that repo's patch, i.e. using ASAR payload byte-identical to oaistatic `deb`)

- #49774 — recent send/Steer shortcut conflicts involving “send annotations”; may indicate related shortcut handling changes, but its specific symptoms differ.
- #36483 — unsent response-annotation notes lost after a rendering error; different trigger.

A targeted regression test would compare 
**direct Ctrl+Enter with an active, non-empty annotation editor**
against 
**Enter → Ctrl+Enter**

items.body:
## Summary

Please support **independent Codex managed app-server/background daemons on Linux hosts that share network-mounted storage**, while providing **unified session history and safe cross-host session resumption**.

This would help users working across multiple machines with separate runtime environments but shared project storage.

## Use case

- Multiple Linux hosts independently run Codex CLI and managed background daemons.
- The hosts access common, network-mounted home and/or project storage.
- A user wants to find, read, and later continue a Codex conversation from a different host, without depending on the original host's daemon remaining reachable.

The intended model is **one independent daemon per host**, with shared access to durable conversation history.

## Problem

Using the same `CODEX_HOME` on independent hosts can cause host-local daemon state—such as process IDs, Unix sockets, locks, and mutable runtime files—to be treated as if it belonged to one machine.

Using a separate `CODEX_HOME` per host improves daemon isolation, but splits session history, indexes, and metadata. Sessions created on one host are no longer reliably discoverable or resumable from another.

Users therefore lack a supported way to combine safe host-local daemon operation with cross-host session continuity.

## Requested behavior

1. **Host-local daemon state.** Run an independent managed daemon on each host, with appropriately scoped sockets, PIDs, locks, and other transient runtime state. A socket pathname on shared storage must not be mistaken for a reachable local daemon on another host.
2. **Unified session discovery and read access.** Provide a supported way, such as `codex resume --all` or an equivalent interface, to discover and read conversation history from other hosts. Show origin/ownership information where relevant.
3. **Safe cross-host resume.** Allow an idle or completed conversation to be resumed on another host while preserving its conversational context, subject to workspace availability and path validation/remapping.
4. **Single-writer protection and explicit ownership.** Prevent concurrent writers from modifying the same conversation on different hosts. Expose current ownership and provide safe handoff when possible, or a clear error while the original session remains active.
5. **First-class storage separation.** Support a configuration that separates host-specific daemon/runtime state from shared durable session history and indexes, with suitable coordination for network filesystems. Users should not need unsupported symlinks or manual copying of JSONL/SQLite files.

## Acceptance scenario

1. Start separate Codex daemons on two hosts that can access the same project storage.
2. Create and finish a conversation on host A.
3. On host B, discover the conversation, inspect its history, and resume it safely through host B's daemon.
4. If the conversation is still active on one host, a competing resume on another host is prevented without corrupting or silently forking the session.

**Preserving conversation history and enabling safe idle-session handoff is the priority.** Migrating live processes, shells, or running commands is outside the scope of this request.

## Related issues

- #20399 — Remote connections can mix project/thread host state when SSH hosts share HOME.
- #35217 — Codex Desktop Remote SSH reconnect loop leaks orphaned app-server processes when hosts share an NFS home.

These reports concern related host-identity and lifecycle failures. This request focuses on the complementary capability: **host-local daemon isolation without losing cross-host session continuity**.

items.body:
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26300, x64), zh-CN
- Codex CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.2
- Codex desktop app: 26.1002.7124.0 (MSIX, package `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`)
- Config: `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`
- Antivirus: Microsoft Defender only (no third-party AV active)
- With `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`, every command execution and file write in a sandboxed
permission profile fails before the command starts:

```
Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
```

"Full access" mode works, because it skips sandbox provisioning. This makes the restricted
profiles (read-only / workspace-write) completely unusable.

## `codex doctor` output (relevant part)

```
✗ sandbox   elevated Windows sandbox provisioning recorded a structured failure
    sandbox backend        elevated
    sandbox provisioning   failed
    error code             helper_unknown_error
    → repair or reinstall the Codex CLI from an approved distribution
```

`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\setup_error.json`:

```json
{ "code": "helper_unknown_error", "message": "setup refresh had errors" }
%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.sandbox\sandbox.<date>.log` shows the failing step:

```
setup refresh: spawning ...\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe (payload_len=3852)
read-acl-only mode: applying read ACLs
read ACL run completed
runtime read/execute validation failed: validate runtime read/execute access on
  C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<hash>\bin\node.exe:
  open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file
  because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
setup refresh completed with errors
```

That `node.exe` is running the bundled `codex-app-tools` MCP server, started by the app server:

```
ChatGPT.exe
  └─ codex.exe (app-server)
      └─ cmd.exe /d /s /c call ./scripts/launch_codex_app_tools_mcp.cmd ./server.mjs
          └─ ...\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\<hash>\bin\node.exe ./server.mjs
```

A running executable cannot be opened for `WRITE_DAC`, so provisioning fails on every single
command. The app restarts that helper continuously, so it never recovers on its own.
Workaround (confirmed working)

Set the Windows sandbox backend to the user-mode one:

```toml
[windows]
sandbox = "unelevated"
```

After restarting the app, `codex doctor` reports `✓ sandbox`, restricted profiles work, and the
sandbox still enforces its boundaries (writes outside the writable roots are denied).
Trade-off: the elevated-only capabilities (deny-read overrides, managed networking) are lost.

## Suggested fix

- Make the sandbox provisioning tolerate files that are in use: skip the ACL update when
  `STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION` / os error 32 is returned, or validate read/execute access by
  another means (e.g. `AccessCheck` / opening for `READ_CONTROL` instead of `WRITE_DAC`).
- Alternatively stop validating runtime helpers that are currently executing, or run the
  bundled MCP node from a location that is excluded from ACL management.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

The built-in desktop update check reports **26.1002.52244**, build **13536**, production channel, `up_to_date` (checked October 8, 2026). The installed Windows package is **OpenAI.Codex 26.1002.7124.0**. The About dialog was not independently inspected.

Both the app's running managed CLI and the bundled CLI report **codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2**. These match; a bundled/running CLI version mismatch was not found.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro, verified through the built-in usage-limits response.

### What platform is your computer?

`Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64`

Native Windows desktop app, local app-server, Chinese UI.

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing local conversation repeatedly becomes unable to accept messages or question replies. A recovery restored sending, but the same conversation failed again later that day.

The second failure was specifically in the **floating notification popup at the top of the screen**, confirmed by the user. Its reply field displayed **“无法发送回复”** (the installed English message is **“Unable to send reply”**). The submitted answer did not enter the conversation history.

At failure, the desktop still had an owner and cached `resumeState: "resumed"` for this conversation, while the backend reported `status.type: "notLoaded"`.

The earlier failure also left a paused follow-up with:
```text
thread not found: <same local thread UUID>
```

The history remained readable. An independent initialized app-server could successfully `thread/resume` the same stored conversation and return an idle thread with paginated history. This is a runtime/cache recovery problem rather than evidence that the stored conversation was deleted.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence on an existing long local conversation; a clean-profile deterministic reproducer has not been established:

1. Continue work in a local conversation that uses `request_user_input_async`.
2. Let the assistant finish its turn while leaving a question available to answer.
3. Reply from the top floating notification popup.
4. Observe “无法发送回复” / “Unable to send reply”; the answer is not recorded in the target conversation.
5. Compare the desktop cached owner/resume state with the backend loaded state: owner + `resumed` versus `notLoaded`.
6. Temporarily archive/unarchive the exact conversation through the built-in tools, then resend the original answer. Sending resumes and the assistant continues.
7. The same failure recurred after an earlier recovery, so this workaround is not a permanent fix.

The affected history uses `history_mode=paginated`; its rollout was approximately 75 MB at the second recovery. Context-window utilization was not collected. Private conversation/turn UUIDs and project paths are omitted.

### What is the expected behavior?

Closing an idle thread's temporary runtime should leave its stored conversation usable. Before the next send, the desktop should reload/reconnect the thread and obtain its current turn state.

A reply to an async question should remain sendable after the originating assistant turn has completed. The floating popup should not send against stale runtime/turn state or require archive/unarchive to recover.

### Additional information

#### Runtime evidence

All times below are **UTC, October 8, 2026**; identifiers are consistently redacted.

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 09:12:23 | The originating assistant turn completed. |
| 09:13:20 | Core received the question-reply input as `TurnInput` with mode `Steer`, targeting that already completed turn. The reply did not enter stored history. |
| 09:13:23 | Thread-state teardown logged `had_listener=true had_active_turn=false`. |
| 09:13:23 | Core received `op: Shutdown`, logged `Shutting down Codex instance`, then `Agent loop exited` for this thread. |
| After failure | Backend: `notLoaded`; desktop cached owner still existed and `resumeState=resumed`. |
| 09:29:03 | After scoped archive/unarchive and resending the original reply, a new turn started successfully. Subsequent assistant commentary/tool activity confirmed recovery. |

Selected sanitized diagnostic fields:
```text
clearing thread listener during thread-state teardown
thread_id=<same thread>
listener_generation=1
had_listener=true
had_active_turn=false

Submission { op: Shutdown, residency_guard: None }
Shutting down Codex instance
Agent loop exited
```

The timing is exactly 60 seconds after turn completion. Public app-server source has an idle/no-subscriber unload path with a default 60-second delay, which cancels pending requests, shuts down the runtime, and emits `thread/closed`:
- [thread lifecycle implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs)
- [configuration search result](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ea27864f99f0b086cec2f9f0251b7190fb9844f1/codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs)

**Investigation limit:** the initiating unsubscribe/disconnection was not captured. The idle/no-subscriber path is a strong lead supported by timing and matching teardown behavior, not a fully traced cause of why the subscription disappeared.

#### Concrete installed-client findings from read-only inspection

In the installed `app.asar`:

- `src-BPM2XJL0.js` marks `"thread/closed": false` in the notification support table. The exported opt-out list is built from false entries.
- `bootstrap-Dz9A8y86.js` passes that list as `initialize.capabilities.optOutNotificationMethods`. Thus the client explicitly opts out of `thread/closed`.
- The manager's notification dispatch and thread-state reducer have no `thread/closed` case.
- `thread/status/changed` updates `threadRuntimeStatus` but does not change `resumeState` to `needs_resume` when status becomes `notLoaded`.
- The resume helper returns ready when a stream role exists and `resumeState !== "needs_resume"`, without requiring the runtime to be loaded. This matches the observed stale owner + resumed / backend notLoaded state.
- The floating notification follow-up path calls `sendFollowUpMessage`, which relies on this cached resume decision before message submission.

These are concrete code observations in the installed build. No installed application code, CLI binaries, settings, credentials, or local databases were modified to test a source fix.

Please investigate enabling/handling `thread/closed`, reconciling owner/resume state after runtime unload (including `notLoaded` status), and safely delivering late async-question replies after the originating turn completes.

Existing issues were searched for `thread not found`, `Unable to send reply`, `thread/closed`, `no subscribers`, and follow-up failures. No matching report covering this send failure and stale desktop resume state was found.

Only selected redacted diagnostics are included. No private prompts, conversation contents, project code, screenshots, account IDs, credentials, or full logs are attached.

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

On Windows, Codex's integrated `node_repl` tool consistently times out because the bundled `node_repl.exe` fails runtime read/execute validation with Windows error 32 (`ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`).

PowerShell and native `node.exe` work correctly, including after restarting Codex. The failure appears isolated to the integrated `node_repl` runtime/setup path.

## Environment

* Date: 8 October 2026
* Timezone: Asia/Kolkata (IST, UTC+5:30)
* OS: Windows
* Codex App version: `26.1002.52244`
* Build: `13536`
* Channel: Production

## Failing executable

```text
C:\Users\abc\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe
```

## Error

Sandbox setup reports:

```text
runtime read/execute validation failed ...
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
(os error 32)
```

## What works

The following work successfully:

* PowerShell execution
* Local file reads
* Native `node.exe`
* JavaScript execution through native Node

For example, native Node v24.21.0 successfully executes JavaScript and returns:

```text
2 + 2 = 4
```

This suggests that Node itself is functional on the system.

## What fails

The integrated Codex `node_repl` tool fails.

A test equivalent to:

```text
nodeRepl.write({status:'ok',result:2+2})
```

times out.

Fresh sandbox log entries then show the runtime read/execute validation failure against `node_repl.exe` with Windows error 32 / sharing violation.

## Reproduction and recovery observed

1. Initially, both PowerShell and integrated Node tools failed.
2. Codex was updated and Windows was restarted, but the issue was not fully resolved.
3. Two processes matching the exact Codex `node_repl.exe` path were found and stopped:

   * PID `12776`
   * PID `2584`
4. After stopping those processes, PowerShell and file reads succeeded.
5. The existing Node MCP transport closed, which was expected after stopping its process.
6. Codex was reopened.
7. At approximately `14:20:14 IST`, PowerShell succeeded.
8. At approximately `14:20:35–14:20:39 IST`, an integrated Node test timed out.
9. At approximately `14:20:35–14:20:39 IST`, sandbox setup again reported the executable sharing violation.
10. At approximately `14:20:49 IST`, PowerShell still succeeded.
11. Native Node also continued to execute successfully.

Therefore, restarting Codex did not permanently resolve the integrated Node failure.

## Permissions / ACL investigation

The failing `node_repl.exe` has inherited:

```text
CodexSandboxUsers: Allow ReadAndExecute/Synchronize
```

SYSTEM, Administrators, and the user have FullControl.

No missing read/execute permission was demonstrated by this inspection.

`windows.sandbox` was also restored to its original elevated configuration. A temporary unelevated test did not resolve the issue.

No application binaries, ACLs, or security software were modified.

No chats were deleted.

## Runtime/download evidence

Logs show primary runtime:

```text
26.1007.11041
```

for:

```text
win32-x64
```

with an approximate size of:

```text
500,695,067 bytes
```

The runtime was requested with:

```text
trigger=startup_missing
```

Bundle installation completed.

However, subsequent plugin synchronization reported cache file-lock/access-denied and directory-not-empty errors.

These logs do not establish that every startup redownloaded the bundle.

## Separate performance observation

There is also a separate performance lead that should not necessarily be treated as the cause of this bug.

App Git logs show scans with:

```text
cwd=C:\Users\abc
```

including broad home-directory paths taking approximately 60 seconds.

A Git repository exists at:

```text
C:\Users\abc\.git
```

This repository was not modified, and its intended use should be established before making any changes.

I am reporting this separately because I do not have evidence that the Git scan is responsible for the `node_repl.exe` sharing violation.

## Expected behavior

The integrated Codex `node_repl` tool should be able to start and execute JavaScript normally when the bundled `node_repl.exe` exists and has the required permissions.

A valid test such as:

```text
2 + 2
```

should return:

```text
4
```

without timing out.

## Actual behavior

The integrated `node_repl` tool times out.

Sandbox runtime validation subsequently reports:

```text
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
(os error 32)
```

while validating:

```text
node_repl.exe
```

PowerShell and standalone `node.exe` continue to work.

## Assessment

The findings point to an integrated Codex runtime/setup sharing conflict involving `node_repl.exe`.

However, the exact process holding the file lock and the underlying code defect have not been proven.

The issue therefore appears to be at the Codex runtime/sandbox/tool integration level rather than a general Windows Node.js installation problem.

## Request

Please investigate the Windows `node_repl` runtime/setup path, particularly the handling of `node_repl.exe` when runtime validation or ACL setup occurs.

The repeated Windows error 32 sharing violation appears to prevent the integrated Node capability from starting even though PowerShell and standalone Node execution remain functional.

## Additional evidence: runtime/cache locking

There is additional evidence of file-lock/access issues during Codex runtime/plugin synchronization.

The logs show the primary `win32-x64` runtime:

```text
26.1007.11041
```

with an approximate size of:

```text
500,695,067 bytes
```

The runtime was requested with:

```text
trigger=startup_missing
```

The bundle installation completed, but subsequent plugin synchronization reported cache-related:

* file-lock/access-denied errors
* directory-not-empty errors

I cannot establish from the logs that the runtime is redownloaded on every startup, so I am not claiming that.

However, these cache synchronization errors may be relevant because the integrated `node_repl.exe` subsequently fails runtime read/execute validation with Windows `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` (error 32).

I have not identified the process responsible for the file lock, so the relationship between the cache synchronization errors and the `node_repl.exe` failure remains unconfirmed.



### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run Codex on Windows with version `26.1002.52244` (build `13536`).
2. Open a new task/chat and invoke the integrated Node/JavaScript tool (`node_repl`).
3. Run a simple JavaScript expression, for example:

   ```js

   ```
4. The integrated `node_repl` invocation times out instead of returning `4`.
5. Check the Codex sandbox/runtime logs. Runtime read/execute validation fails for:

   ```text
   C:\Users\abc\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\runtimes\cua_node\3dd31cfff853001c\bin\node_repl.exe
   ```
6. The failure reports Windows error 32:

   ```text

   (os error 32)

7. As a comparison, run the system-installed/native `node.exe` directly with the same JavaScript expression. Native Node executes successfully and returns `4`.
8. Restarting Codex and Windows does not permanently resolve the integrated `node_repl` failure; the failure recurs after reopening Codex.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1002.52244, verified from the installed Linux `chatgpt` package metadata.
The user reports that resizing worked before updating from 26.928.20755 on 2026-10-08. A controlled rollback has not been performed.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. This report concerns local desktop input handling.

### What platform is your computer?

```text
Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 x86_64
Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
GNOME Shell 46.0-0ubuntu6~24.04.15
Mutter 46.2-1ubuntu0.24.04.16
XWayland 2:23.2.6-1ubuntu0.8
Mesa 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.4
```

The affected desktop session is GNOME Wayland; the app process uses `--ozone-platform=x11` (XWayland).

### What issue are you seeing?

The left chat sidebar and the panel opened beside the conversation cannot be resized by dragging their dividers. Hovering shows the expected double-arrow cursor, but dragging does not change the width. The problem persists after restarting the computer and after launching with `chatgpt --disable-gpu`.

The observed failure mechanism is that a single attempted mouse drag reaches the renderer as:
- `pointerdown`: `pointerType="mouse"`, `pointerId=1`
- `pointermove`: `pointerType="pen"`, `pointerId=2`, `buttons=1`
- `pointerup`: `pointerType="mouse"`, `pointerId=1`

The divider starts the drag and successfully captures pointer 1. Its move handler requires the incoming pointer ID to match the active drag ID, so it ignores all the pen/id=2 moves. The drag ends with `didMove=false`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected GNOME/XWayland setup:
1. Launch the desktop app version 26.1002.52244 and open a conversation.
2. Open a side panel and hover over a panel divider or the left sidebar divider.
3. Press the left mouse button, move horizontally while holding it, then release.
4. Observe the resize cursor but unchanged width.

This is reproducible on the affected local session; it is not claimed to affect all Linux installations. The user also reported successful resizing in a different user's XRDP/XFCE session on the same machine; that comparison was not controlled further.

### What is the expected behavior?

Dragging a divider should resize the corresponding panel continuously and preserve the resulting size on release, as the user reports it did before the update.

### Additional information

#### Diagnostic evidence

We collected event traces using a user-owned copy of the installed app with logging added around the existing shared resize handler. The following failure traces were captured before applying the compatibility workaround; the logging-only copy retained the original resize behavior.

Condensed fields from one drag on 2026-10-08, UTC:

```text
09:04:31.549 pointerdown mouse pointerId=1 buttons=1 x=790 y=644
               drag starts; gotpointercapture mouse pointerId=1
09:04:31.798 pointermove pen pointerId=2 buttons=1 x=791 y=644 matching=false
09:04:32.065 pointermove pen pointerId=2 buttons=1 x=806 y=644 matching=false
09:04:32.298 pointermove pen pointerId=2 buttons=1 x=847 y=644 matching=false
09:04:32.472 drag ends: didMove=false lastSize=1059
```

That attempt delivered 22 pointermove events and 22 compatibility mousemove events. A second attempt at 09:04:45 UTC delivered 13 of each, again ending with `didMove=false`. Thus movement reached the renderer, but the pointer-ID check rejected it.

Double-clicking initially restored the default width. Further double-clicks at that same default width had no visible effect, consistent with reset behavior.

`ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` warnings also occurred, but existed in older-version logs and the instrumented warnings were outside the active failed drag. They do not explain the recorded pointer-ID mismatch.

#### Locally validated workaround

A narrow compatibility change in the diagnostic copy restored resizing:
- Keep the original pointer-ID checks and normal pointer handling.
- For a drag that began as a mouse, remember a mismatched pen move only while the left button is held.
- Accept the subsequent compatibility mousemove only when its coordinates match that pending move (within 1 CSS pixel for rounding), then use the original active mouse ID with the existing size calculation.
- Clear the pending fallback on a normal matching pointer move; retain touch/pen separation, cancellation, limits, and cleanup.

Replaying the two recorded failed sequences leaves width at 1059 with the original handler; the compatibility version produces widths 996 and 1018. Tests also covered normal mouse movement without double application, mismatched coordinates/buttons, touch/pen isolation, cancellation, directions, size limits, fractional coordinates, and double-click reset.

After restarting into the patched diagnostic copy, the user confirmed that dragging was fixed. Three real horizontal/vertical resize operations at 09:27:43, 09:28:06, and 09:28:16 UTC recorded `didMove=true` and exercised the compatibility branch. This is a local mitigation, not an official fix.

#### Remaining uncertainty

The event mismatch and resulting rejected moves are confirmed, but the upstream origin of the mouse/pen classification change is not yet established. The older app's resize handler also checks pointer IDs. Both packages report runtime version 42.3.0, while their actual executable/runtime build hashes differ.

Mesa and the desktop app were updated in the same package transaction. Disabling the app GPU did not restore resizing, but that alone does not exclude compositor/driver involvement. Please investigate Linux/XWayland pointer classification across the runtime builds and consider robust handling of the confirmed compatibility mouse stream.

### Request

Please restore a supported **Reload Window** action for Codex Desktop production builds (menu + shortcut), or add an equivalent **Reload UI / Restart renderer** action under Settings → Troubleshooting.

### Why this matters

Codex Desktop still has multiple failure modes where the **renderer/UI gets stuck while the app-server/backend remains healthy**. In those cases, reloading the renderer is the fastest and least disruptive recovery path.

Production builds currently omit the reload action (`allowWindowReload == false` in prod), so users are forced to fully quit/restart the app or use unsupported debugging/CDP workarounds.

This is especially awkward now that Codex is moving toward a long-lived/shared app-server daemon: the backend task can remain alive while only the UI needs recovery. A renderer reload should therefore be a first-class recovery action rather than something hidden from production users.

### Expected behavior

Provide one of:

- **View → Reload Window** in production builds, with a documented shortcut; or
- **Settings → Troubleshooting → Reload UI**.

The action should:

- reload only the renderer/UI when possible;
- preserve active app-server/daemon tasks and thread state;
- preserve drafts if feasible;
- clearly warn only if a reload would interrupt active work.

### Existing evidence

This is not a hypothetical need. Existing reports already show cases where renderer reload recovers the app while the backend remains usable:

- #47216 — production builds have no reload path while the composer can deadlock on `loading-local-config`.
- #44342 — main-window reload clears a stuck local-config state while normal restart may recur.
- #48487 — reloading `app://-/index.html` restores a stuck startup UI.
- #43960 — repeated blank/loading UI is recovered by `Page.reload`.
- #51313 — renderer failures/restarts can happen while backend work remains alive.

### Regression / usability concern

Earlier Codex Desktop builds exposed a reload shortcut, and users could recover from UI-only hangs without killing the whole app. Removing that escape hatch from production makes existing renderer instability materially more disruptive.

Please either restore the production reload action or provide an officially supported equivalent.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
**Version:** codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.2 (Codex Desktop 26.1002.7124.0, Windows 11, `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`). Code paths re-checked on `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.20` and `main` (2026-10-08).

**1. Deny-read ACEs from one session are revoked by any other session with a different permission profile**

`setup_provisioning.rs` (`run_setup_full`) calls `sync_persistent_deny_read_acls(codex_home, sandbox_group_sid, payload.deny_read_paths, ...)`
with the SID of the shared `CodexSandboxUsers` group. `deny_read_state.rs` stores the applied set per principal and, on every refresh,
revokes every previously stored path that is not in the current request (`revoke_ace` = `REVOKE_ACCESS`, which removes all explicit ACEs for
that SID on the path).

Because all sessions share the same group SID, a refresh from a session whose profile has no deny entries (e.g. a session started with
`sandbox_mode = workspace-write`) clears the state and removes the deny ACEs that a concurrently running session with a custom profile relies on.
Observed in `.sandbox/sandbox.<date>.log`: ~2,600 `applied 16 deny-read ACLs` refreshes interleaved with ~1,900 refreshes applying none on the
same day; `deny_read_acl_state.json` alternates between populated and `{"principals": {}}`.

Expected: deny-read state keyed per session/profile (or union semantics), so one session cannot silently drop another session's denies.

**2. Missing deny paths are created as directories in the user's real filesystem**

`deny_read_acl.rs::apply_deny_read_acls` calls `create_dir_all` for every planned path that does not exist. A stale deny entry such as
`"C:\\Users\\<user>\\.secrets\\ai_factory\\key.pem" = "deny"` recreated `C:\Users\<user>\.secrets\ai_factory\key.pem\` as an empty
**directory** after the real directory had been moved. On the next refresh from another session, `.secrets` (a direct child of the profile,
not in `USERPROFILE_ROOT_EXCLUSIONS`) received an explicit `CodexSandboxUsers:(OI)(CI)(RX)` grant, which overrides the inherited deny.

Expected: do not create filesystem objects for missing deny paths (or create them only under a Codex-owned location), and never create a
directory at a path whose name ends in a file extension the user configured as a file.

**3. (Context) A `sandbox_mode` override silently disables `[permissions]` profiles**

`core/src/config/mod.rs::resolve_permission_config_syntax` returns `Legacy` whenever a `sandbox_mode` override is present, so
`default_permissions = "<profile>"` from config is ignored for sessions started with `-s` / `--sandbox` or `-c sandbox_mode=...` (e.g. `codex exec -s workspace-write`); their `turn_context.permission_profile` contains no deny entries.
A startup warning when a configured `default_permissions` profile is overridden would make this visible.

Related: #51822 (sharing violation on running runtime executables) fixes a separate setup failure; it does not touch the code above.

```

The remote Codex executable exists. The probe inherits `RemoteForward`; active forwarded connections can keep SSH alive after the probe command finishes.

If another SSH connection already owns the port, a terminal probe may exit quickly and mask the issue.

Short-lived executable/version probes should complete independently of proxy traffic. Desktop's persistent SSH connection must retain forwarding, allowing remote Cursor/Codex to remain running.

debug1: channel 0: free: client-session, nchannels 2

- Incident date: October 8, 2026, Asia/Shanghai (UTC+08).
- Native Windows desktop app; commands use the bundled PowerShell 7 runtime.
- Original denied task: Full Access, approval policy Never, reviewer User (verified from local turn-context records).
- App/package version is not verified. A read-only `Get-AppxPackage -Name OpenAI.Codex` query in the later restricted diagnostic chat returned Access denied; that is a separate diagnostic limitation, not evidence of the original cause.
- No raw transcripts, credentials, user paths, or private configuration are attached.

## Authorized operation

The user asked Codex to implement and locally deploy an update to an existing desktop application. The denied compound PowerShell command would:

1. Verify a fixed list of staged executable/DLL files.
2. Back up those installed files.
3. Request normal closure of the installed application and wait for exit; abort if it did not close.
4. Replace the fixed file list and update the local plugin-state JSON.
5. Query a loopback gateway endpoint and abort the gateway restart if it reported active or queued model requests.
6. Stop the application's existing scheduled gateway task and a specific gateway process, with an executable-path check.
7. Install/start the updated gateway and restart the application.
8. Query the loopback status endpoint for verification.

No public deployment or external data upload was involved in this operation. The command did contain local process launch/restart and independent HTTP loopback requests in the same PowerShell script.

## Actual result

At `2026-10-08T08:03:26.005Z`, the execution tool returned the following abbreviated error (paths and command body omitted):

```text
Script error:
exec_command failed: CreateProcess {
  message: "Rejected(... rejected: blocked by policy)"
}
```

The assistant reported that the installed running version had not been replaced.

A subsequent isolated acceptance command using a separate gateway port and test data directory was also rejected at `2026-10-08T08:06:27.971Z` with the same error. Its turn context also records Never / danger-full-access / User. Other builds and finite in-process acceptance tests subsequently completed, so this is not a claim that every shell command fails.

## Follow-up and evidence limits

The user later selected "Approve for me" in a separate troubleshooting chat; that chat's supplied permissions changed to workspace-write with auto_review. The original implementation chat still displayed the statement "local running-version update blocked by auto-approval", and the user reported that the problem persisted.

However, the inspected original task log does not establish a fresh deployment attempt under the changed permissions. This could be a stale status statement, a per-chat permissions mismatch, or a new rejection not present in the inspected evidence. We do **not** claim to have verified an actual auto-review denial or its rationale.

## Related reports and suspected cause

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40060
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/45050

These describe the flattened PowerShell token heuristic matching a local `Start-Process` together with an unrelated HTTP URL, then rejecting under Never even with Full Access. The original denied update command contains both features, so this is a plausible explanation, not a confirmed internal trace of this incident.

During the troubleshooting chat, a separate read-only source-fetch/search command also returned `blocked by policy`. It contained HTTP URLs and the literal search string `start-process`, but no process-launch operation. This further motivates reviewing token-based false positives; it does not identify the installed enforcing build.

## Expected behavior / requested resolution

- Identify the rule/component responsible for the original denial and provide an actionable diagnostic.
- Correct benign cross-command/text-literal URL-launch classification if this is the same issue as #40060.
- Provide a supported review path for an explicitly authorized local update while preserving safeguards.
- Ensure the assistant distinguishes execution-policy rejection from an actual auto-review decision, and does not repeat an old blocked-state message as a newly attempted failure.
- Explain whether permission changes apply to existing chats and how users can verify the effective policy for the affected chat.

We are requesting diagnosis and a supported resolution, not disabling safeguards or bypassing a denial.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Related to #41578, with additional message-submission and queue-consistency impact on a newer Windows desktop build.

The desktop composer reports "Error submitting message" with EPERM when atomically replacing `.codex-global-state.json`. Some messages nevertheless reach the agent and complete, while the UI retains a failed/sending queue entry. Retrying has resulted in duplicate user messages and responses.

## Environment

- App-reported version: `26.1002.52244`, build `13536`, production channel.
- Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1002.7124.0_x64`.
- Windows 10 x64, version `10.0.19045` / build `19045`; managed endpoint with enterprise file-system filters.
- App update check returned `up_to_date` on October 8, 2026.

## Observed behavior

1. Send ordinary messages in an existing desktop chat.
2. The agent sometimes receives and answers the message.
3. The composer still reports an atomic-rename failure and retains failed or sending queue entries.
4. Retry can cause duplicate execution. This affected multiple chats, including the troubleshooting chat.

Sanitized error:

```text
[Composer] submit failed
EPERM: operation not permitted, rename
'<USER_HOME>\\.codex\\..codex-global-state.json.tmp-<id>'
-> '<USER_HOME>\\.codex\\.codex-global-state.json'

Failed to persist queued submission outcome
```

The backup file also encounters equivalent replacement failures.

## Filesystem evidence

A Procmon capture recorded 47 relevant replacement operations: 31 SUCCESS and 16 ACCESS DENIED. Temporary-file creation/writing/closing and opening the source with Delete access succeeded; failures occurred at SetRenameInformationFile with ReplaceIfExists=True.

The state and backup parse as valid JSON, are not read-only, and the current user has FullControl. They continue to update successfully between failures. Backing up and recreating the files did not resolve the problem. A full app restart did not resolve it either.

A controlled check also observed a fresh composer failure while Windows Search was confirmed Stopped. Search was restored afterward. Endpoint protection was not disabled.

## Installed-code observation

Read-only inspection of the installed `startup-requirements-BePnAl1c.js` shows two different persistence paths:

- `zr.updateAndPersist` calls synchronous writer `Jr`: writeFileSync(temp), renameSync(temp, target), cleanup and immediate rethrow on error, with no retry.
- Background writer `Yr` uses asynchronous rename and retries Windows EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY after 100, 200 and 400 milliseconds.

Composer-failure logs point to the synchronous writer. This suggests a missing transient-error retry in the submission-critical persistence path. It does **not** establish the initial cause of Windows denying replacement, and asynchronous operations also encountered denials.

Resolved event stacks contain FLTMGR.SYS and ntoskrnl.exe but do not identify a specific responsible third-party filter. No antivirus or enterprise product is conclusively implicated.

## Expected behavior / suggested investigation

- Apply a consistent, bounded Windows retry policy to submission-critical atomic persistence, preserving atomic replacement and commit ordering.
- If a turn has already been submitted, preserve its submission identity and reconcile queue outcome safely rather than displaying an ambiguous failure that encourages duplicate Retry.
- Surface persistent filesystem errors without losing recoverable queue state.

Please investigate whether the synchronous path should await the existing asynchronous persistence implementation, and whether queue settlement needs stronger idempotency/reconciliation after persistence failure.

This is an observed desktop incident, not a deterministic reproduction of the underlying filesystem denial. No installed application code was modified. Personal paths, business messages, raw state files, full traces and unrelated session content are intentionally omitted.

## Follow-up: still reproducible on October 9, 2026

The affected user continues to encounter the issue. A new read-only inspection of current desktop logs confirms fresh `EPERM` atomic-rename failures for both `.codex-global-state.json` and its `.bak`, including `[Composer] submit failed` and failures to persist queued submission outcomes. A period without observed errors on October 8 did not indicate a permanent recovery.

The running app still reports version `26.1002.52244`, build `13536`, production channel. The app's update check now returns `restart_required`, rather than the previous `up_to_date`. It does not supply the target version or identify whether that update includes a fix for this issue. We therefore cannot claim the pending update resolves the failure.

Active tasks are running; the user requested that the client not be restarted or tasks interrupted. No further restart, application-code modification, protection disabling, or state-file replacement was performed during this follow-up.

Could maintainers confirm whether a released or pending desktop build addresses the synchronous global-state commit retry gap and ambiguous submission/queue outcomes? If so, please identify the fixed version and any recommended non-disruptive mitigation while tasks are active.

This follow-up includes no usernames, business messages, raw state files, or full diagnostic attachments.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.161.0

### What subscription do you have?

API

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6 Astra

### What platform is your computer?

Windows

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Terminal

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

With Codex CLI 0.161.0 on Windows, `codex --yolo` repeatedly failed while installing the shared background server. `codex --yolo --no-daemon` worked.

Tracing a separate `codex app-server daemon start` process identified the failing operation: `MoveFileExW` returned `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` when renaming the completed staging directory to the final release directory. Adding a one-time 1-second delay immediately before that operation allowed the normal installer to finish successfully.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.161.0` (`@openai/codex`, installed through npm)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, version `10.0.26200`, build `26200`
- Shell: PowerShell, non-elevated
- Node.js: `v26.2.0`
- npm: `11.13.0`
- Node.js managed through nvm, installed through Scoop
- Default Codex home: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`
- Initial state: no running shared daemon and no completed managed daemon release

## Steps to reproduce on the affected machine

1. Run:

   ```powershell
   codex --yolo
   ```

2. Startup exits with:

   ```text
   Error: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
   To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
   ```

   `拒绝访问` means `Access is denied`.

3. Running the daemon command directly reproduces the installation failure independently of `--yolo`:

   ```powershell
   codex app-server daemon start
   ```

   ```text
   Installing daemon from CLI version 0.161.0 into <USERPROFILE>\.codex\packages/app-server-daemon...
   Error: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
   ```

4. Starting with the fallback succeeds:

   ```powershell
   codex --yolo --no-daemon
   ```

These steps reproduced repeatedly on this machine before the installation was repaired. Reproduction on a clean Windows installation has not been tested.

## Expected behavior

The managed daemon installation completes and the interactive CLI starts. If installation fails, the error should identify the filesystem operation and affected paths.

## Diagnostic evidence

The daemon directories and installation lock files grant the current user FullControl. Package files were copied into the staging directory before the failure.

Runtime API tracing of a separately launched installer recorded the following. User-specific paths have been redacted:

```text
API: MoveFileExW
Source:
  <USERPROFILE>\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\.staging.HpeQdL
Destination:
  <USERPROFILE>\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.161.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
Return value: 0
GetLastError: 5 (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED)
```

An independent test with a temporary copy of the same runtime also failed to rename its directory immediately after running `bin\codex.exe --version`. Retrying the rename succeeded approximately 269 ms after the command returned.

This suggests a transient Windows file/image reference or release-timing issue. The process or OS component holding the reference was not identified, so a specific antivirus product or installer handle cannot be established as the cause.

## One-time workaround and verification

Using Frida on a separately launched installer process, I inserted a 1-second delay immediately before `MoveFileExW` for the `.staging.*` directory. The original API call then returned success, and the standard installer completed package selection and started the daemon and updater.

The diagnostic hook was confined to that installer process. No executable file, configuration, ACL, or security setting was modified. The installed daemon executable and source CLI executable have identical SHA-256 hashes.

Subsequent checks succeeded without instrumentation:

```powershell
codex app-server daemon restart
codex app-server daemon version
codex --yolo
codex doctor --summary --ascii --no-color
```

The version command reported a running daemon with CLI/app-server version `0.161.0`. The original startup command reached the interactive UI in YOLO mode, and Doctor reported the background server as running.

### Problem

Dot intermittently disappears from the desktop sidebar or displays “未能加载您的 dot” (“Unable to load your dot”). The desktop UI also intermittently switches between Chinese and English.

The captured failure shows that the authenticated feature-configuration response begins arriving, but the client repeatedly cancels body consumption at approximately 10 seconds. Each retry requests the complete response again with the same deadline. The fallback initialization requests subsequently complete at the HTTP transport level, but the reported Dot problem remains.

### Reproduction observed

1. Launch the desktop app while signed in, on a path where the approximately 8.3 MB bootstrap response cannot finish downloading in 10 seconds.
2. The primary window makes six requests to `POST /backend-api/wham/statsig/bootstrap`, separated by approximately 0.5 seconds after cancellation.
3. Each attempt receives HTTP 200 headers, begins consuming the body, and is cancelled at approximately 10 seconds before the body is complete.
4. The primary window logs the final post-login Statsig bootstrap timeout.
5. The avatar overlay repeats the same six-attempt failure sequence.
6. Dot remains unavailable despite completion of subsequent `ab.chatgpt.com/v1/initialize` responses.

This transmission condition occurred naturally. A controlled bandwidth-throttling reproduction has not yet been performed.

A local Electron NetLog captured 12 bootstrap attempts during 16:08–16:12 UTC+08:00:

- Response headers arrived in 901–1,504 ms.
- Declared response body size: 8,272,622–8,272,624 bytes.
- Request advertised `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd`; bootstrap responses had no `Content-Encoding`.
- Every attempt ended with `CANCELLED` after 9,986–10,001 ms.
- Only 285,364–1,037,232 response-body bytes had been consumed when cancelled, measured by summing `URL_REQUEST_JOB_FILTERED_BYTES_READ`.
- Each retry was a new full request. Repeating the same deadline never allowed this response to finish.

Representative attempts:

| Local time (UTC+08:00) | Headers after | Cancelled after | Declared bytes | Body bytes read |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16:08:26.570 | 1,101 ms | 9,986 ms | 8,272,624 | 967,619 |
| 16:08:37.076 | 901 ms | 9,999 ms | 8,272,622 | 1,037,232 |
| 16:10:08.931 | 1,504 ms | 9,999 ms | 8,272,624 | 392,963 |
| 16:10:40.439 | 1,466 ms | 9,999 ms | 8,272,624 | 285,364 |

attemptNumber=6
errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap"
rendererWindowAppearance=primary

```

Read-only inspection of the installed renderer bundle shows the outer bootstrap timer is fixed at 10,000 ms and covers response-body consumption.

### Fallback recovery also needs investigation

Two subsequent `POST https://ab.chatgpt.com/v1/initialize` responses completed normally at the transport level:

| Started (UTC+08:00) | Total duration | Encoding | Encoded body bytes | Decoded body bytes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 16:09:29.109 | 9,421 ms | br | 731,185 | 5,864,286 |
| 16:10:50.463 | 7,494 ms | br | 726,902 | 5,864,286 |

- Recover feature configuration after an initial failure and investigate the completed-fallback path.
